title: Duo acceptance: live workspace to collisions
intro: Everything built since the live workspace (Phase E) through organising, Send to Claude, local HTML with the element picker, duo2 parity, Claude editing open documents, and collisions with changes on disk. Open Duo on the fixture workspace first: run `scripts/acceptance/open-duo.sh` in the duo-v2 repo. Fixtures live in ~/DuoAcceptance (rebuild with `scripts/acceptance/fixtures.py --reset`). Each test has a Set up test button (Duo arranges the fixtures) and, where Claude ran it first, what Claude did and what still needs your judgment. Updated 2026-10-04 evening with everything since (DL-82 to DL-98): Duo opening on every session, Home, folder columns, the Open-then-past list, untitled names, tasks and session links.
setup: In a terminal: `cd ~/repos/duo-v2 && scripts/acceptance/open-duo.sh` (it adds any new fixtures without resetting yours)
duo2 commands: use `~/repos/duo-v2/build/Duo.app/Contents/Helpers/duo2` from a normal terminal, or plain `duo2` inside a Duo session's terminal (or anywhere, once you accept the install question).
Several Send items need a Claude session showing: open checkout and click `+ New session` first.

decisions.title: A keyboard shortcut for Send Selection to Claude
context: **Send Selection to Claude** puts the text you've selected (in a Markdown document or an HTML page) into the showing Claude session's prompt, quoted with its file and lines, without sending. Today it's in **Edit › Send Selection to Claude** and on the right-click menu, with no shortcut.
The shortcut map is locked (DL-34): every chord needs a decision. All Duo chords carry ⌘ so they never collide with keys typed into Claude Code. Chords already taken:
`⌘K` jump · `⇧⌘A` search · `⌘↑` All projects · `⇧⌘H` Home · `⇧⌘P` peek · `⌘↩` jump into the peek's selection
`⌃⌘S` sidebar · `⌥⌘0` right pane · `⌥⌘←/→` panes · `⌘N` / `⇧⌘N` new file / folder · `⌘S` save · `⌘B` / `⌘I` bold / italic · `⌘W` / `⇧⌘W` close tab / window
plus macOS's own: `⌘F` find, `⌘Z` undo, `⌘C/V/X`, `⌘A`, `⌘Q`…

Legacy Duo used **⌘D** for exactly this (its "Send → agent" pill), so your fingers may already know it. ⌘D is free in Duo. In the macOS Save dialog ⌘D means "Don't Save", which can't clash with a document view.
This choice can also be Search's "Send to Claude" shortcut (decision 23e), so one chord means send everywhere.
